answer: Under EigenTrust, reputation follows the normalized trust matrix and reciprocity-weighted transitivity, with an exponential temporal half-life that discounts stale evidence. Durable influence therefore requires sustained honest service, not a burst of activity. A freshly spawned identity—whether called opal or linked as a bridge—has negligible incoming trust and near-zero eigenvector centrality; a small delta in account count cannot lift it past consensus thresholds without trusted interactions.
